assertions.subject: a TLS-era instance is installed as the thing to be upgraded
assertions.expected: install PASS, certs directory populated, all four soon-to-be-removed keys present in its configuration
assertions.control: the acceptance run applied the same four-key detector to the new installer output and found 0 of them
assertions.note: This is the shape a real site is upgrading from, not a hand-written approximation of it.

assertions.subject: the machine-scope variable the upgrade is asked to clear exists before the upgrade
assertions.expected: CONTROL_SERVER_TICKET09_PROBE_CERT_PASSWORD present with the value this run generated
assertions.note: Value never printed. Without this precondition the clearing segment would trivially "pass" by having nothing to do.

assertions.subject: a package that passes the manifest check but cannot start is not silently accepted
assertions.expected: the upgrade throws, and the diagnostic log shows it got past backup-complete before failing
assertions.actual: threw=True steps=preflight-complete>service-stopped>backup-complete>staging-complete removedKeys=4 healthUrlRewritten=True>certificate-cleanup-complete directory=True password=True>replacement-installed>failure: Service '8005 AGV ControlServer Ticket09 Legacy (8005 AGV ControlServer Ticket09 Legacy)' cannot be started due to the following error: Cannot start service '8005 AGV ControlServer Ticket09 Legacy' on computer '.'.>rollback-complete
assertions.note: Failing before the backup would prove nothing about rollback; the manifest hashes were regenerated so the tamper survives preflight.

assertions.subject: rollback puts the original installation back byte for byte
assertions.expected: 0 differences between the install tree before the upgrade and after the rollback
assertions.control: the same comparer reports the differences introduced by the successful upgrade later in this run (must be non-zero there)

assertions.subject: rollback restores the machine-scope certificate password it cleared
assertions.expected: the probe variable holds the same value it held before the failed upgrade
assertions.note: This is the segment ticket 03 could not execute at all.

assertions.subject: the instance is running again on its original binaries after rollback
assertions.expected: service Running and the certificate directory restored from the backup

assertions.subject: the documented section 4.5 upgrade completes on a real TLS-era installation
assertions.expected: result PASS, service Running, sourceCommit equal to the new candidate

assertions.subject: the upgrade removes the certificate directory from the data root
assertions.expected: reported removed AND C:\Users\szy\w2g-ticket09\upgrade\data\certs absent on readback
assertions.control: LEGACY-INSTALL recorded 3 files in that directory before the upgrade
assertions.note: Ticket 13 note applied: the reported field is the script talking about itself, so the readback is the evidence.

assertions.subject: the upgrade clears the machine-scope certificate password it was pointed at, and only that one
assertions.expected: the probe variable is gone and the production variable still holds its original value
assertions.control: PROBE-VARIABLE-SET recorded the same variable present with a known value minutes earlier in this run
assertions.note: Both halves matter: clearing everything named like a certificate password would also satisfy the first half alone.

assertions.subject: the retained production configuration is migrated to the plaintext key set
assertions.expected: all four removed keys gone, Health:url rewritten to http
assertions.control: LEGACY-INSTALL found all four of those key names in this same file before the upgrade

assertions.subject: the upgrade actually replaced the installation
assertions.expected: the same comparer that reported 0 differences after rollback reports differences here
assertions.note: This is the control for UPGRADE-ROLLBACK-RESTORES-INSTALL: the comparer is shown to be capable of reporting a difference.

assertions.subject: the upgraded instance answers /health/live over plain HTTP
assertions.expected: 200 with status live at the migrated Health:url
assertions.control: the same endpoint on the same port spoke HTTPS before the upgrade; the legacy install verified it with curl --cacert

assertions.subject: no key material survives under the upgraded install and data roots
assertions.control: the same detector over the backup root still finds the legacy material the rollback path depends on: 6 (must be non-zero)
assertions.note: The backups are inside the disposable run root and go away with it; a production upgrade leaves them under the backup root on purpose.

assertions.subject: the upgrade does not claim to have removed the CurrentUser\Root certificate
assertions.note: Manual section 4.5 carries the manual removal; reporting it as cleaned here would be a false green.

assertions.subject: the rehearsal instance is removed
assertions.expected: service absent, install root and data root removed

assertions.subject: the probe machine-scope variable does not outlive the rehearsal
the whole rehearsal leaves the certificate stores as it found them
assertions.expected: 0 of the 4 observed stores changes its sorted-thumbprint digest
assertions.note: The legacy installer creates its root and leaf in CurrentUser\My and deletes both after export; -InstallCurrentUserRoot was deliberately not passed.

assertions.subject: the production service and its machine-scope secret survive the rehearsal
assertions.expected: no drift against the pre-run snapshot (PID 8632, ::1:58007 127.0.0.1:58005 127.0.0.1:58007) and the certificate password unchanged
assertions.note: The entire point of -CertificatePasswordVariable: this assertion would fail if the rehearsal had used the production name.
